tutorials.title: Troubleshooting fundamentals
tutorials.summary: Follow one complete Observe → Diagnose → Isolate → Repair → Verify → Document path using the real local authority.

checkpoints.title: Observe separate information surfaces
body: The selected Ticket shows reported Symptoms and public Candidate faults, not the hidden answer. The queue changes which Ticket is displayed.
Machine state summarizes authorized change. Evidence records findings; the Worklog is the immutable accepted-action sequence. They are related, but they are not interchangeable.

checkpoints.title: Read turn resources before acting
body: A turn opens with two Actions. Test, Command, Repair, and Verify costs appear on their Cards. Bench diagnostics persist; response Cards come from the private hand and move to discard after use.
Search spends an Action and token to fetch a named response Card. Refresh spends an Action and token to recover eligible discard Cards. Pass ends the turn when you need fresh Actions or a draw.

checkpoints.title: Record a working hypothesis
body: Open the full Ticket and choose any Hypothesize control. A hypothesis is a private/team notebook belief, not a submitted guess, and changing it gives no truth feedback.

checkpoints.title: Run a diagnostic with no candidate effect
body: Select Visual Inspection on the persistent Bench, confirm that this displayed Ticket is the target, and submit it. A clean, negative, unrelated, or inconclusive finding is still recorded Evidence; no candidate effect is explicit feedback, not a missing result.

checkpoints.title: Interpret Evidence without overclaiming
body: SUPPORT raises a candidate without proving it. CONTRADICT weighs against it. RULE_OUT supports a notebook elimination. CONFIRM is candidate-specific and decisive. INCONCLUSIVE records that the run did not decide the question.
Rule out/reinstate is a free, cited, revision-bound notebook action. A remaining Candidate is not automatically true, and a CONFIRM for a non-actionable condition does not open Repair.

checkpoints.title: Collect supporting context
body: Run RAID Status Inspection on the displayed Ticket. Its result supports the failed member and can also confirm the non-actionable degraded-array condition; Repair remains locked until an actionable Fault has an accepted Isolation.

checkpoints.title: Ask why Isolation is unavailable
body: Open the full Ticket and expand “Why can’t I isolate?”. The guidance uses only your authorized projection: phase, public dispositions, projected citations, eliminations, and generic next steps.

Direct observation, definitive diagnostic, corroborated support, evidence-backed elimination, and recovery-derived routes are distinct authored routes. An unsupported attempt stays generic so it cannot distinguish a wrong Candidate from insufficient Evidence.

checkpoints.title: Collect decisive actionable Evidence
body: Run Drive Health Test. Its candidate-specific CONFIRM is decisive for the actionable failed member. The result remains attached to this Ticket and current diagnosis revision.

checkpoints.title: Commit the supported Isolation
body: Open the full Ticket and Isolate the candidate confirmed by the latest Evidence. The engine chooses authorized citations for its real route. Evidence can come from several Players, but one accepted event owns this Fault and stage.

checkpoints.title: Repair changes machine state
body: Use Replace RAID Member from the response hand. If it is not held, use Search and then Pass for enough Actions. The Card goes to discard and machine revision changes; success is not proven until Verify.

checkpoints.title: Verify the named requirement
body: Use RAID Health Verification after the Repair. Verify checks the named post-Repair condition; a pass must be current for the latest machine revision. Failure or inconclusive results would remain in history and return the Ticket to Diagnosis.

checkpoints.title: Preserve the path, then close
body: Document Live publishes an eligible accepted action into the Worklog without closing the Ticket. Final Document & Close submits the complete closure bundle, locks the Worklog, settles eligible contribution points, and archives the Ticket.

Help can replay these explanations. Give Up instead abandons one Ticket, voids pending contributions, records the statistic, reveals its authoritative solution privately, and allows any remaining queue to continue.

checkpoints.title: Publish one live Worklog entry
body: Open the full Ticket and choose one Document Live control. The original accepted action remains unchanged; publication enriches its Worklog entry.

checkpoints.title: Document and close the Ticket
body: Choose Document & Close. The engine independently validates the accepted Isolation, decisive Evidence, necessary Repair, current passing Verify, and preserved history before closure.

tutorials.title: Failed Verify and recovery
tutorials.summary: Repair one real fault, preserve a failed Verify, return to Diagnosis, and complete the second valid recovery path.

checkpoints.title: Begin with a plausible first path
body: This authored Ticket contains a real two-stage causal repair path. You still begin from public Symptoms and Candidates; the guide never reads hidden truth from the active projection.

checkpoints.title: Collect array status
body: Run RAID Status Inspection on the displayed Ticket to record supporting Evidence for the failed member.

checkpoints.title: Confirm the first actionable fault
body: Run Drive Health Test. Its public candidate-specific CONFIRM supplies the decisive first-stage Evidence.

checkpoints.title: Accept the first Isolation
body: Open the full Ticket and isolate the candidate confirmed by the latest Evidence.

checkpoints.title: Replace the failed member
body: Use Replace RAID Member. Search, Refresh, or Pass are available when needed; the Repair itself remains an ordinary legal engine intent.

checkpoints.title: Run the Verify that exposes unfinished recovery
body: Use RAID Health Verification. The real authored result fails: the member is online, but the degraded array still needs a distinct Isolation and rebuild.

checkpoints.title: Read the preserved recovery state
body: The Ticket is Returned to Diagnosis with a new diagnosis revision. Earlier Evidence, the accepted Isolation, machine-state change, failed Verify, and Worklog remain historical rather than being erased.
The failed Verify created authorized Evidence that CONFIRMs the second public Candidate. That current-stage finding activates a recovery-derived Isolation route.

checkpoints.title: Commit the recovery-derived Isolation
body: Open the full Ticket and isolate the Candidate confirmed by the failed Verify Evidence.

checkpoints.title: Rebuild the isolated degraded array
body: Use Rebuild RAID Array. This is a second machine-state change owned by the second accepted Isolation, not a retry of the first Repair.

checkpoints.title: Verify the recovered current state
body: Use RAID Health Verification again. This current pass satisfies the requirement after the latest Repair; the earlier failure remains preserved.

checkpoints.title: Close with the complete recovery history
body: The closure bundle must include both accepted stages, both necessary Repairs, the failed Verify, and the current passing Verify. Optional or redundant work would remain history; it is not retroactively declared illegal.

checkpoints.title: Publish one recovery entry
body: Open the full Ticket and publish one eligible accepted action with Document Live.

checkpoints.title: Document and close the recovered Ticket
body: Choose Document & Close. The authoritative engine validates and archives the complete two-stage path.
